subject.title: [Feature]: cron add: support custom job IDs via --id

question: Should OpenClaw make custom cron job IDs a supported public create-time contract across `cron add`, Gateway RPC, and agent-tool cron creation, and what exact validation/collision rules should it use?
rationale: This adds a user-controlled identifier to a public cron creation API, so automation should not choose the permanent ID contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept custom IDs with a narrow contract
options.body: Add optional slug-like IDs, preserve UUID generation when omitted, reject duplicates explicitly, and update all public create surfaces plus docs and generated clients.

options.title: CLI-only experiment
options.body: Expose `--id` only in the CLI while keeping broader Gateway and agent-tool support deferred, reducing API scope but creating an uneven contract.

options.title: Keep UUID-only creation
options.body: Close the feature direction and rely on list/show/edit workflows to discover IDs instead of supporting human-chosen IDs.

recommendation.title: Accept custom IDs with a narrow contract
recommendation.body: Add optional slug-like IDs, preserve UUID generation when omitted, reject duplicates explicitly, and update all public create surfaces plus docs and generated clients.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron create ergonomics and service/CLI history make this the strongest product/API routing signal among the observed owners.
